Grammys 2026: 'Sword of the Sea' Wins Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media and More
Austin Wintory composed the score for Sword of the Sea.
Sword of the Sea, developed and published by Giant Squid, won Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media at the 2026 Grammys.
The award, listed under Category 73, honours composers for an “original score created specifically for, or as a companion to, video games and other interactive media.” Austin Wintory, who composed the music for Sword of the Sea, took home the Grammy Award, beating titles such as Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora – Secrets of the Spires and Helldivers 2.
Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media – Nominees List
- Sword of the Sea — Austin Wintory, composer - WINNER
In the Best Song Written for Visual Media category, Golden from Netflix’s KPop Demon Hunters won the award. The song was written by EJAE, Park Hong Jun, Joong Gyu Kwak, Yu Han Lee, Hee Dong Nam, Jeong Hoon Seo, and Mark Sonnenblick. It was performed by HUNTR/X, featuring EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and REI AMI.
Best Song Written for Visual Media – Nominees List
- Golden — From KPop Demon Hunters — EJAE, Park Hong Jun, Joong Gyu Kwak, Yu Han Lee, Hee Dong Nam, Jeong Hoon Seo & Mark Sonnenblick, songwriters (HUNTR/X: EJAE, Audrey Nuna, REI AMI) — WINNER
Ryan Coogler’s Sinners also had a strong showing at the 2026 Grammys. The film won Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media, beating A Complete Unknown, F1 The Album, KPop Demon Hunters, and Wicked. It also won Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media (Film and Television). Other nominees in the category include How To Train Your Dragon, Severance: Season 2, Wicked, and The Wild Robot. Meanwhile, the 2024 documentary Music By John Williams won the Best Music Film award.
You can check out the complete list of winners and nominees from the 2026 Grammy Awards.
FINAL: Austin Wintory won Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media at the 2026 Grammy Awards for his composition on "Sword of the Sea"
